Many ancient Greek philosophers wrote at length about marriage. They weren't Christians and they weren't homophobes either. They never considered homosexual relationships to constitute a marriage, because a marriage is one thing and a homosexual coupling is something else. Ancient Greece, from which we draw much of our philosophical and cultural foundation, was neither Christian nor homophobic, and never, not in their laws, customs, or in the writings of their philosophers, held homosexuals relationships to be a basis for marriage. The reason is simple. They held the same view of marriage as we did until 40 years or so ago - the conjugal view.

Marriage means different things to different people nowadays. Throughout the entirety of history of Western civilization, from the Ancient Greeks until roughly the past 40 years or so, the universally held concept of marriage was the conjugal view - that marriage exists as a permanent and exclusive union between a man and a woman for the purpose of bearing and raising a family, for the benefit of children, and through this, for society. A deep friendship does not such a marriage make. A life partnership doesn't either. Not even if it includes homosexual sex.

Today we have a competing idealization of marriage, invented over the past 40 years or so (and mostly by straight people, certainly). This view holds that marriage and family raising are two separate things, and marriage exists for the benefit of the wedded couple. If this is what marriage means to us, then it certainly makes sense that two men or two women can be married and have their marriage endorsed by the state. I'd argue that it also makes sense for 3 women, or 5, or really any number to be married. State endorsement of gay marriage codifies and solidifies this view, and the abandonment of the conjugal view. This view will now be enforced by law. This is a threat to traditional man-woman conjugal marriage and family raising.

I don't expect to change your mind about the issue. The argument is this: Traditional marriage is the most beneficial arrangement for doing society's most important work. State endorsement of gay marriage equals state endorsement and enforcement of a definition of marriage, which - despite eye rolling from enlightened John Stewart followers everywhere - does immediately and directly threaten traditional marriage.

This is not a religious position. This is a secular argument. I was not raised with religion and it's never occurred to me to get one. I don't understand the enthusiasm for gay marriage. You're all going to feel awfully naive when the polygamy battle, which is next, begins.

I'm a 16 year old hobbyist game developer from the Netherlands. Here's a wall of text about the things I am doing.

I actually have never really finished a game other than some small crappy Unity gamejam games. Like this one. Now that I'm replaying it I realized that the turrets can kill enemies as well, I didn't even program that in.

But I have 3 projects going on at the moment. One is a sequel to Vinesauce Joel's Barbecue Quest, which I am using as an excuse to write an implementation for R^5 RS Scheme as a scripting language.

Another one is a Vlambeer-inspired side-scrolling shooter which will focus heavily on upgrades and gun customization. I kind of want it to be like Clicker Heroes but with actual gameplay. So you kill enemies to get points, and then you can use those points to upgrade your stuff. And the more you upgrade, the more damage you deal, which means you kill more enemies and can upgrade more again.

And lastly my biggest project, which I actually have screenshots of, a side-scrolling shooter with way too many features.

I began with the idea of destructible terrain and implemented that using Minecraft-like chunks made out of pixels, I then got the idea to use Run Length Encoding to merge the pixels into rectangles and it worked really well. Because rectangles mean that I don't have to batch each individual pixel, but I can just batch the rectangles and it will be much faster. And collisions can just use the same rectangles.

The idea is that it's going to be kind of Deus Ex like, as in that you have multiple ways to do an objective. I think it would be fun to make it so that you can use the destructible terrain to your advantage. Like digging a tunnel under some enemies so that they don't spot you, or crushing your enemies with big chunks of terrain.

And for the screenshots: (Excuse the debugging stuff)

  • https://slimgur.com/image/WF4

  • https://slimgur.com/image/WFU

Explanation of the debugging stuff:

  • The flames are a test of a particle system thing I wrote

  • The "Useful debugging stuff goes here" are some variables to test player movement.

  • The red polygon on the second image is an area where explosions do 50% damage to terrain, I made a quad-tree-esque system that uses arbitrary N-gons instead of squares to handle that.

  • The green crosshair on the first image is a test of a procedural locomotion system that is currently broken as shit.

I'm currently working on a level editor, and thinking of a way to do structural integrity in a fast and biased way.

And by the way, I am making the engines for all 3 games by myself, because engine development is really fun.

But enough about my projects. I hope /v/gamedev and /v/programming will take off soon.
